findings.title: MMD converges linearly to its magnetic fixed point where GDA cycles
findings.claim: On symmetric zero-sum matrix games, fixed-magnet MMD exhibits linear (geometric) last-iterate convergence to its fixed point, while simultaneous GDA cycles, bounded away from equilibrium.

findings.title: Uniform-anchor MMD fixed points differ from logit-QRE for asymmetric games
findings.claim: For asymmetric games, MMD dynamics converge to an attractor distinct from logit-QRE(λ=1/τ), exhibiting context-dependent attractors.

findings.title: Regularized Nash Dynamics reach Nash universally
findings.claim: MMD with periodic reference resets converges to Nash (NashConv < 0.05) on symmetric AND asymmetric games.

findings.title: DEQ peak activation memory is O(1) in effective depth
findings.claim: DEQ implicit block: 0.032±0.000 MB peak activation memory, flat across effective depth; explicit stack: linear at 0.0168 MB/layer. At N=32: DEQ 0.032 MB vs explicit 0.539 MB (~17× reduction).

findings.title: Anderson acceleration beats Picard on stiff fixed points
findings.claim: Anderson achieves <0.95× Picard iterations at ρ=0.999 (0.888 at dim 32; 0.940 at dim 128), validating theory. No advantage at easy ρ.

findings.title: Second-price auction is exactly truthful; weighted aggregation is manipulable
findings.claim: Second-price: regret 0.0 (CI [0.0,0.0]). Weighted aggregation: regret 0.0773 (n=3), 0.0683 (n=5) — non-truthful.

findings.title: Warm-started homotopy accelerates QRE path tracing
findings.claim: Warm-starting reduces solver iterations: 25.2% on asymmetric 2×2, 2.6% on biased RPS; matching pennies flat (degenerate control).

findings.title: Undamped logit-QRE requires damping for high rationality
findings.claim: Plain softmax(λAs) diverges at λ>0.32 on biased RPS. Adaptive damping converges across λ∈{1,10,100} in 21/700/42k iterations.

findings.title: Tier B EqLM pipeline validated end-to-end (SMOKE)
findings.claim: ExplicitLM+AdamW learns (125→4.39 loss); EqLM+AdamW learns slowly (132→28.5); EqLM+raw-MMD stalls (128→125) due to optimizer confound. BLiMP scores are noise at this scale; pipeline works.

findings.title: EqLM matches explicit transformer at smoke scale after init fix
findings.claim: With correct init (all arms start at CE 10.82–10.83 = ln|V|), EqLM+AdamW reaches final loss 5.94 vs ExplicitLM 5.99 over identical 800-step budgets — parity — with 6.2% fewer parameters, at 2.7x wall time.
caveats: MagneticAdamW arm throttled learning (10.83→9.91) — tau/EMA coupling mis-tuned
MagneticAdamW peak memory 97.7GB vs 3.5GB — memory bug
DEQ solver 0% convergence at max_iter=12/tol=1e-3 during training yet training succeeds — phantom-gradient regime

findings.title: exp05 token-budget description was wrong (data cap)
findings.claim: exp05 iterations 2–3 cycled a 22,703-unique-token corpus (the 1000-sample cap, F9 blocker) for ~3.3M token-PRESENTATIONS — not 3.3M unique tokens. The F10 parity claim remains valid as a like-for-like comparison, but describes an overfitting-regime corpus.
findings.note: Cap fixed in kinetic_ai/data/dataset.py; exp06 onward uses real stream

findings.title: MagneticAdamW coupled-weight-decay bug
findings.claim: Folding weight decay into the gradient before Adam normalization makes wd·θ act as a ~lr-magnitude decay on parameters whose gradients are mostly zero (tied embedding rows). Decoupling wd restores EXACT AdamW equivalence.
findings.lesson: optimizer-equivalence tests must include sparse-gradient parameters; dense-Linear tests masked defect

findings.title: Magnetic pull (τ≤1e-2) is loss-neutral at pretraining scale; solver budget beyond 12 iters buys nothing
findings.claim: On real data stream (300 steps), magnetic arms (τ∈{1e-4,1e-3}) reached 8.52–8.61 vs explicit baseline 8.51 (within 10% prereg: MET). Solver budgets {12,24,48} → loss {8.60,8.67,8.67}; 0% convergence at tol 1e-3 in all budgets — phantom-gradient regime is loss-neutral.
findings.drift_prereg: MIS-DESIGNED (compared EqLM arms to explicit-architecture baseline) — recorded as invalid, not 'missed'
findings.tier_b_decision: pretraining arms use AdamW (A1/A2); MagneticAdamW with FIXED reference reserved for H3 (preference-phase)

findings.title: H1 iteration 1: MISSED at scale; diagnosis points to non-contractive fixed-point map
findings.claim: Full-run (20k steps, param-matched, 2000-pair BLiMP on 1000 scored pairs): A1 ExplicitLM loss 3.90/BLiMP 0.734; A2 EqLM 4.42/0.571; A3 EqLM+MagneticAdamW(1e-3) 4.68/0.584. EqLM = 78–80% of baseline BLiMP vs pre-registered ≥95% → **H1 iter-1 MISSED**. DEQ solver converged 0% at tol 1e-3 across all budgets ⇒ non-contractive fixed-point map (spectral norm never wired into EqLM).
findings.diagnosis: DEQ solver converged 0% of forward passes at tol 1e-3 across all budgets (exp06b) ⇒ block's fixed-point map is not contractive. Smoke 'parity' (F10) held only in 22.7k-token cycled corpus (memorization regime). At scale, lack of contraction-enforcement breaks learning signal propagation.
findings.wall_time: EqLM 3.5 hours vs ExplicitLM 1.2 hours (2.9x slower); peak memory comparable (~3.5–4.7 GB)
findings.next_iteration: EqLM-v2: enforce contraction via spectral norm on block weights / pcDEQ constraints; verify >80% solver convergence; rerun matched comparison. Secondary: solver-tol study (1e-2 vs 1e-3), solver depth warmup.

findings.title: EqLM's map has no bona fide fixed point: weight-tied iterated transformer, not equilibrium model
findings.claim: Solver residual plateaus at constant value with tail-ratio ≈0.99. Residual magnitude scales LINEARLY with damping α: 32.65 → 5.41 → 1.35 at α = 1 / 0.2 / 0.05. Signature of z ← z + α·g(z) with ‖g‖ constant: iterates drift at speed α‖g‖, no fixed point approached. Trained 'EqLM' models are 12-iteration weight-tied transformers, not equilibrium computation.
findings.discovery: Absolute global norm convergence criterion was unsatisfiable at batch scale. Root cause: outer LayerNorm placed after the implicit map, not within it. Iterates not bounded, fixed points do not exist. Reframing F13: BLiMP 0.571/0.584 quantify weight-tying at matched parameters, not equilibrium.
findings.status: VALIDATED · sign-off pending · discovery via exp07

findings.title: EqLM-v3 (post-LN map): fixed points now exist but contraction is weak at LM width (H1 frontier identified)
findings.claim: v3 with f(z,x)=LN(z + Attn + MLP + inj(x)) (Bai et al. DEQ-Transformer form) restores bona fide fixed points. Direct probe at full smoke width (d=204, T=127, 80 iters): relative residual decays 1.0 → 0.105 monotonically then creeps (0.1078 → 0.1053 over last 24 iters). F14 constant-speed-drift signature ELIMINATED (bounded iterates, genuine approach), but effective contraction factor ≈1 at width, so tol 1e-2 is unreachable in practical iteration budgets.
findings.interpretation: Architecture question H1 poses is now precise: make the post-LN transformer map strongly contractive at width WITHOUT destroying capacity. This is the identified scientific frontier of the program.
candidate_v4_directions: Tighter spectral budget on attention value/projection paths only
pcDEQ orthant constraints on activation magnitudes
Tolerance-sufficiency study: does rel 0.1 suffice for representation quality?
findings.status: VALIDATED · sign-off pending · H1 iteration 2 remains open — this is the identified scientific frontier

findings.title: Solver-aware auxiliary loss teaches contraction almost for free (BREAKTHROUGH; resolves F15 frontier)
findings.claim: Adding L = CE + λ·r with r = ‖f(z*,x)−z*‖/‖z*‖ (one tracked application after no-grad solve) reduces exit relative residual 16× (0.1277 → 0.0076–0.0078) for every λ ∈ {0.01, 0.1, 1.0}, at ≤1.8% CE cost (8.92–8.99 vs control 8.77) and zero wall-time overhead (0.99–1.00×). The post-LN map becomes a genuine equilibrium computation (rel residual ≪ 1e-2 target) — the model LEARNS to be contractive.
findings.consequence: H1 iteration 2 unlocked: full 20k-step matched comparison with EqLM-v4 (post-LN + aux λ=0.01) now possible.

findings.title: H1 iteration 2: post-LN EqLM reaches 94.4% of baseline BLiMP (near-miss, within noise); aux loss trades capacity for contraction at scale
findings.claim: EqLM-v4 post-LN no-aux reaches 0.704 BLiMP = 94.4% of ExplicitLM baseline 0.746 (loss 4.45 vs 3.75). This is 0.6pp below pre-registered 95% threshold, but within 1σ (binomial σ ≈ 1.4pp at n=1000 pairs): statistically a TIE with threshold, seeds required to adjudicate. EqLM-v4 with aux λ=0.01: 0.658 BLiMP (loss 4.43) — solver-aware loss, ≤1.8% CE cost at 300 steps (F16), costs ~4.6pp BLiMP compounded over 20k steps: contraction and task capacity trade off at fixed λ. Iteration-1→2 progress: EqLM 0.571 → 0.704 via arch fixes alone (post-LN map + init scaling). Wall time 2.9×; memory parity.
findings.next_step: 2 more seeds of A1/A3 to resolve near-miss with mean±CI (CLAUDE.md ≥3-seed gate)
findings.status: VALIDATED · seeds pending for H1 verdict

findings.title: H1 verdict (3 seeds): EqLM reaches 93.0% of the explicit baseline's BLiMP — formally below the 95% threshold (HONEST MISS with a tight CI)
findings.claim: Seeds 42/43/44, 20k steps each, full stream, param-matched: A1 explicit BLiMP 0.7133±0.0294 (0.746/0.689/0.705); A3 EqLM post-LN 0.6637±0.0365 (0.704/0.654/0.633). Per-seed ratio 0.944/0.949/0.898; mean 0.9303, 95% bootstrap CI [0.8979, 0.9492] — upper bound < 0.95 ⇒ pre-registered H1 threshold MISSED. Paired bootstrap: Δ=+4.97pp for explicit, p<1e-3, effect size 1.84. Trajectory of program: iteration 1 ratio 0.78 → iteration 3 ratio 0.93 via diagnosed fixes (init scale, post-LN fixed-point map). Memory parity at this scale; wall time 2.9×; O(1) depth-memory advantage retained (F4).
findings.paper_position: A weight-tied equilibrium LM attains 93% of a param-matched explicit transformer's BLiMP at equal token budget — reported with the full diagnostic arc (F13–F17) and the open gap as future work (eval-time solver budget, aux annealing, multi-block DEQ).
findings.status: VALIDATED (formal H1 miss) · closes RQ-3 iteration 3

findings.title: Warm-started equilibrium decoding cuts solver cost 79% at 97.6% token agreement (H1'a: reduction PASS, agreement narrow miss; smoke scale)
findings.claim: Initializing each decode step's solver from the previous token's equilibrium reduces mean iterations-per-token by 79.3% (7.91 → 1.64, target ≥50% PASS) at 97.6% token agreement (976/1000), 39/40 sequences exact. Greedy agreement narrowly misses ≥99% prereg (one divergent sequence); knob for scale run available.
findings.significance: Validates TRIZ P10 prediction: sequential equilibria are geometrically close. This INVERTS wall-clock story — explicit L-layer stack always pays L applications/token; warm equilibrium model pays ~1.6 at smoke scale. Unique architectural advantage impossible for explicit stacks.

findings.title: exp10 Probe: Memory advantage and loss lead appear at 110M matched parameters (early observations, full run in progress)
findings.claim: Early probe (300 steps, 121–124M params matched): EqLM peak memory 6.2GB vs explicit 8.0GB (−22% — O(1)-depth advantage first visible at LM scale); EqLM AHEAD on training loss (6.79 vs 7.40 at step 275, same random init). Wall-clock 5.6× slower (2.57 vs 0.46 s/step). Full 10k-step run in progress.
findings.observations: Loss reverses small-scale pattern (EqLM ahead, not capacity-traded). O(1)-depth memory advantage proven at scale. Wall-clock driven by 12 fixed-point iters/forward — F19 warm-start will be critical for decode efficiency.
findings.status: PROBE — early observations only · full 10k-step run in progress

findings.title: At 121M parameters the truncation penalty widens with width: quality ratio 0.787, memory −23%
findings.claim: Across 3 seeds at 121M matched params (10k steps, full BabyLM stream), EqLM reaches 78.7% of the explicit baseline's BLiMP (CI [0.785, 0.788]) while confirming the O(1)-depth memory advantage (6.29 vs 8.13 GB). The fixed-point solver exhausts its 12-iteration budget at every width tested; width raises the price of that truncation (7% gap at d=204 vs 21% at d=1704). Adversarial review corrected the initial 'convergence fails at scale' reading — the effect is graded contraction loss, not binary failure.

findings.title: H3 PARTIAL: the magnet under-doses at pre-registered tau — but DPO damages unseen phenomena, and EqLM is 1655x more drift-resistant
findings.claim: MPO (DPO + magnetic pull to the frozen base) exactly matches DPO's held-out accuracy at pre-registered tau (displacement ~2e-5, under-dosed; dose-response rider running). Secondary: DPO lifts trained phenomena 0.646->0.877 while unseen phenomena drop 0.740->0.612 (KL 1.24 nats/token); the equilibrium model under identical updates drifts 1655x less (0.00075 nats/token) via damped gradients through the weight-tied solve.

findings.title: H4 MET (3/3 seeds): truthful token-auction selection beats the best single specialist by 23% on mixed-domain perplexity
findings.claim: Second-price per-token auction of two 30M domain specialists (childes vs simple_wiki): mixed-stream perplexity 182.8 vs 236.8 best single and 207.9 logit-average ensemble; bids are target-independent confidence, mechanism cross-checked (0 mismatches). Scoped per adversarial review: teacher-forced scoring-time selection (not yet autoregressive generation); absolute childes ppl may reflect split overlap; traces are a 200-position sample.

findings.title: H5 MISSED (3/3): the auction's teacher-forced advantage inverts in closed-loop generation - and the judge metric itself is style-dominated
findings.claim: Closed-loop greedy generation from mixed prefixes: best single specialist 3.4-3.7 judge-NLL beats auction 4.2-4.7 on all seeds (F22's scoring-time rescoping empirically vindicated). Per-domain decomposition reveals the BabyLM-trained judge carries a ~2-nat childes style prior larger than any between-system effect, so the verdict is scoped judge-relative. Judge-free observations: the auction has the lowest repetition of all systems (0.39-0.48); the uniform ensemble degenerates (0.78-0.83).

findings.title: H6 PARTIAL - with parity: anytime-unrolled training closes the ENTIRE width gap (ratio 0.991 vs explicit at 121M); certification achieved separately; naive combination refuted
findings.claim: B1 (CE supervision on plain iterates z4/z8/z12, Anderson-solver eval) hits BLiMP 0.662/0.697/0.672 - ratio 0.991 vs the explicit baseline, one seed above it - and trains 2.1x FASTER than solver-based training. Budget-sweep rider MET (graceful degradation at Anderson budgets 4/8/12). B2's trajectory-local penalty delivers the first certified 121M equilibrium (conv 1.0 at 4.0 iters) at a quality cost. B4 (naive combo) refuted at 0.529. Open problem sharpened: quality-preserving certification.

findings.title: The baseline ladder, and the thinness of subject-level headroom
findings.claim: Measured on one harness, the parameter-matched comparison is not the strongest player: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct leads MMLU at 0.626 against Qwen3-1.7B's 0.583. Council members win disjoint subjects, yet an aggregator granted advance knowledge of the best player per subject gains only 0.96 points over always using the strongest.
findings.note: GSM8K excluded: strict match scored zero for every model, which measures the answer convention an instruction-tuned model emits rather than whether it can do the arithmetic.

findings.title: The influence game does not beat averaging at answer level, and confidence is the reason
findings.claim: Over 8,301 questions the best of 45 influence-game settings scores 0.6311 against uniform averaging's 0.6304, at a standard error of 0.0053. Accuracy falls monotonically as influence concentrates, by eight points at the largest rationality tested. Influence follows agreement with the consensus, which measures confidence rather than competence.

findings.title: Eleven aggregation rules, none better than the mean, and the reason
findings.claim: Mechanism design and calibration both fail to repair the game. Pricing a player's proposal by what it is worth to everyone else scores 0.6257 (paired z = -2.63); the median 0.6144; Borda 0.5922. Per-player temperature calibration cuts expected calibration error from 0.151 to 0.037 without moving the aggregate. Every rule reweights one fixed body of evidence, and the game discards part of what a council with a twenty-point ceiling cannot afford to lose.
findings.verdict: NOT MET; closes the answer-level arena
